subject: Clarify quantized billing / rounding impact on hybrid calls — Acme pilot
messages:
From: Lisa Tran <lisa.tran@acmeretail.com>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick billing question before PO

Hi Avery,

Thanks again for yesterday's walkthrough. Procurement asked us to confirm one technical billing detail before we cut the PO — specifically how Redwood's billing quantum and minimums interact with our hybrid usage pattern. We have two main call types during the pilot:

- "Search + generate" flow (server call that attaches a 5k-token context, then a streamed 1k-token generation)
- Frequent short chat calls (under 100 tokens) used by agents for lookups

Can you confirm whether: 1) the 5k context gets rounded up to the nearest quantum for the chargeable context bucket, and 2) streaming generation is billed per-streamed token or per-call minimum? Procurement is worried about a large rounding uplift for context-heavy calls and a separate minimum for every small chat call.

I attached our internal estimate spreadsheet and a one-pager. A plain example with numbers would help the PO reviewer.

Thanks,
Lisa
Lisa Tran
Head of ML Integrations, Acme Retail
Attachments: acme_pricing_questions.pdf (pdf), pricing_calc.xlsx (xlsx)
From: avery_johnson@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 13:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick billing question before PO

Hi Lisa — thanks for the clear ask and the spreadsheet. Short answer up-front: context and generation are billed separately and both use a 512-token quantum for metering in your pilot region; streaming tokens are billed per-token (subject to the same 512-token rounding rule for invoicing), and short chat calls are subject to the per-call minimum when they fall below the quantum.

Concrete example (so procurement has something to paste into the PO):

- 5,000-token context -> rounding: ceil(5000 / 512) * 512 = 5120 billed tokens for context.
- 1,000-token streamed generation -> ceil(1000 / 512) * 512 = 1024 billed tokens for generation.
- Total billed tokens for that composite call = 5120 + 1024 = 6144 tokens.

Small chat example: a 60-token request -> ceil(60 / 512) * 512 = 512 billed tokens (so you'll hit the per-call quantum).

Notes/nuance:
- We meter context separately from generation so you won't double-count the same tokens, but both sides round up independently.
- For continuous streaming where a single long generation is split across frames, totals are summed then rounded once at the invoice-line level (not per-frame) — so fragmentation doesn't multiply rounding.
- Pilot concession options are possible; happy to propose something so the initial months don't see disproportionate rounding uplift.

Looping in Marissa for a quick proposal we can offer to Acme so procurement can approve the PO.

Best,
Avery
Avery Johnson
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Subject: FW: Quick billing question before PO

Avery/Ben — see Lisa's ask. My quick take below, plus two concession options and rough math so the finance reviewer can see impact. I attached a mock invoice row in the attachment.

Assumptions for the calculation:
- Quantum = 512 tokens (per Avery)
- Unit price = $0.0008 per token (generation) / $0.0003 per token (context) for pilot pricing in us region (rounded for example)
- Expected pilot volume: 1,000 hybrid calls over 30 days + 25k short-chat calls

Baseline math (no concession):
- Hybrid call (avg): context 5,000 -> billed 5120 * $0.0003 = $1.536; gen 1,000 -> billed 1024 * $0.0008 = $0.8192 -> total $2.3552 per hybrid call
- For 1,000 calls -> $2,355.20
- Short chat 60 tokens -> billed 512 * $0.0008 = $0.4096 per call -> for 25k calls = $10,240
- Total monthly pilot bill ~ $12,595.20 (rounded)

Concession options to propose to Acme:
1) Rounding credit for first 3 months: apply a token-credit equal to rounding delta (i.e., billed_tokens - actual_tokens) on context buckets only. Practically reduces the 5k->5120 delta of 120 tokens per hybrid call. Example delta saving: 120 * $0.0003 = $0.036 per hybrid call -> $36 for 1k calls over month. Small but symbolic.

2) Minimum-waiver for chat pilot: waive quantum minimum for short chat calls under 128 tokens for pilot months (i.e., bill actual tokens up to 128 instead of full 512). This materially reduces the 25k short-chat line. Example: 60-token chat would be billed at 128 tokens -> 128 * $0.0008 = $0.1024 vs $0.4096 -> saves ~$0.3072 per chat -> ~$7,680 over 25k calls.

Recommendation: offer option 2 for the pilot (big impact) and option 1 as a goodwill credit. If Ben signs off on finance, we can come back with a short amendment for the PO.

-Marissa
Senior Pricing Analyst, Redwood Inference
Attachments: pricing_calc.xlsx (draft)

Agree with Marissa. Option 2 (minimum-waiver under 128 tokens) is a clean pilot concession — low risk and shows good faith. A couple of implementation notes for ops/billing:

- Add a pilot flag on the account so metering applies the waiver during the pilot window (2026-07-01 -> 2026-09-30).
- Keep invoicing lines transparent: show actual_tokens, billed_tokens, rounding_delta, and any pilot_credit line so Acme sees the math.
- For the formal amendment, let's cap the waiver exposure: maximum waiver credit of $10k for the pilot. After that we revert to standard quantum.

If that's acceptable, I'll draft a one-paragraph amendment and sign-off the finance cap.

Ben Carter
